explainBack.question: Why doesn't the September 10 signing mean a companion chatbot must already have the one-hour session limit and disabled push notifications today?
explainBack.answer: Because signing enacts the law but the specific duty sections (21812, 21812.5, 21813) only become operative on July 1, 2027. Until that date the legal requirement does not yet apply, so an operator has an implementation window, not an immediate obligation; audits start on a still-later clock, January 1, 2029 or first public availability, whichever is later.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must cite the operative-date concept (P003, P012), the specific defaults (P005), and the separate audit timetable (P008).
explainBack.assessment: The article supports this answer fully in ordinary language; a reader could reconstruct the causal chain from P003, P005, P008 and P012 without outside knowledge.

unseenTransfer.scenario: In November 2026, a small California startup (about $40 million in annual revenue) launches a companion chatbot with push notifications on by default and no session limits. A parent asks whether the company is already breaking Adam's Law and whether an independent audit will catch it soon.
unseenTransfer.question: Is the startup violating the law today, and when would an audit apply to it?
unseenTransfer.answer: It is likely not yet violating the operative duties: the default-settings and session-limit requirements in Section 21812 do not apply until July 1, 2027, so today the company is inside its implementation window rather than in breach. And the audit section will not reach it soon: with under $500 million in prior-year revenue, the operator is exempt from that audit section until 2032, so no independent audit is due before then regardless of the general 2029 deadline.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Correct application requires the operative date (P003), the default settings (P005), and the audit timing plus revenue exemption (P008).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism handles this new scenario completely; both the timing and the exemption transfer cleanly, confirming genuine mechanism understanding rather than headline recall.

signing.reason: The Padilla release states Newsom signed SB 1119 on September 10, 2026, and AP independently reports the September 10 signing of the package including this law.

scope.reason: The enrolled text's Section 21812 imposes child-safety duties on operators making companion chatbots available in California, matching the article's scope statement.

operative-date.reason: The enrolled text states Sections 21812, 21812.5 and 21813 become operative July 1, 2027, matching the article's 'main child-safety sections' framing.

risk-assessment.reason: Section 21812 requires a documented child-safety risk assessment before a new or substantially modified chatbot is released, with documented reasonable mitigation, exactly as reported.

settings.reason: The enrolled text specifies parent-controlled defaults disabling push notifications and limits of one continuous hour and two total hours per day, matching the article.

memory-exception.reason: The enrolled text says persistent conversational memory is ordinarily disabled by default with a qualified exception for users 16 or older when specified guardrails are implemented, as the article states.

prohibited-behaviours.reason: The listed behaviours (self-harm encouragement, sexual/romantic content, sentience claims, emotional reliance, disproportionate praise, evading parental controls) match the enrolled text; the article's paraphrases ('excessive praise', 'hide use from parents') are faithful.

family-context.reason: AP reported the law was inspired by Adam Raine's story and quoted Maria Raine on parents' understanding of AI-companion risks; the article attributes both correctly to AP.

audit-timing.reason: Section 21814 sets the first audit deadline at January 1, 2029 or before first public availability, whichever is later, exactly as reported.

audit-exception.reason: The enrolled text exempts operators with under $500 million in prior-calendar-year gross revenue from the audit section before January 1, 2032, matching the article's 'until 2032'.

status-lag.reason: The source records the status pages showing 'presented to the Governor' as of September 9 when checked; the article adds that this persisted 'even after' the signing release, a timing claim slightly stronger than the excerpt, though the substance (lagging record, not a veto) is fully supported and correctly bounded.
